result.summary: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md in full, then read apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible/withdrawRegistration and apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts's isAutoPromotionHalted line by line against the design, plus handlers/withdraw.ts and domain/user.ts's new getUserForNotificationById. Lock discipline (AC4, the concurrency-critical property): confirmed `SELECT id, status, starts_at, ends_at, capacity FROM events WHERE id = eventId FOR UPDATE` (registration.ts lines 368-378) is the literal FIRST statement inside promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible -- no prior read, no prior write. Confirmed withdrawRegistration (lines 499-565) never itself locks the events table -- its own FOR UPDATE (lines 508-518) is only against the registrations row being withdrawn; the events-row lock happens exclusively inside promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible, called from withdrawRegistration's own tx (line 560), never a nested db.transaction. Deadlock-order check, worked through myself rather than accepting the design's prose: withdrawRegistration's lock order is registrations(withdrawn row) -> events -> registrations(waitlist candidate, a DIFFERENT row, step 4's FOR UPDATE, lines 409-415); registerForEvent's lock order is events -> registrations(caller's own (event,user) row, via its later UPDATE/INSERT -- the existing-row SELECT at lines 145-149 is NOT itself FOR UPDATE, so the actual lock is taken later, at write time). The only resource contended by both transactions is the single `events` row -- a single shared resource cannot produce a wait-for cycle regardless of ordering elsewhere, so no new deadlock potential. Confirmed. NEW concurrency scenario, independently constructed (not copied from BACKEND-DEV's own AC4 case): wrote a throwaway test file apps/bot/src/domain/_reviewer_scratch_promotion_concurrency.test.ts (deleted immediately after use, git status --porcelain confirmed clean) -- TWO concurrent withdrawals from the SAME capacity-2 event (both admitted seats withdrawn via Promise.all against a shared waitlist of exactly 2 people, distinct created_at). Ran 15 iterations against the already-running scratch Postgres (bot-postgres-1, port 55432): PASS all 15 -- both withdrawals always returned {kind:'withdrawn'} with promotion.kind='promoted' every time (never 'no-waitlist', never 'capacity-full'), the two promoted userIds were always the two distinct waitlisted users (Set size 2, matching the two seeded waitlist users exactly -- no double-promotion of the same candidate, no lost promotion), post-state always showed exactly 2 admitted rows and 0 waitlisted rows for the event. This exercises step 4's per-row FOR UPDATE (the candidate-selection lock) under real contention on a SHARED waitlist, which BACKEND-DEV's own AC4 test (a single withdrawal racing a single fresh registration) does not cover. Re-ran BACKEND-DEV's own AC4 test myself, not trusted from the report: `TEST_DATABASE_URL=... npx vitest run apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts -t AC4 --reporter=verbose` -> PASS, 815ms, 20/20 iterations, admitted-row count never exceeded 1. AC1-AC7 independently re-verified by reading the actual test code (registration.db.test.ts, handlers/withdraw.test.ts) against the domain implementation, then re-running the whole suite myself under the mandated `--no-file-parallelism` flag (a first attempt running the two files together WITHOUT that flag produced deadlocks/FK-violation noise from concurrent TRUNCATEs across separate connections -- confirmed this was a file-parallelism artifact of my own ad hoc invocation, not a real defect, by re-running with the correct flag and getting a clean pass; not filed as a finding since it reproduces only when the documented command is not used): AC1 -- 48h-out event (isAutoPromotionHalted(startsAt,eval) = false since 48h>24h, matches §2.1's boundary), capacity full, 3 waitlisted rows at created_at+1s/+2s/+3s: withdrawal promotes exactly the first (regA) via the (created_at ASC, id ASC) tie-break at step 4, confirmed admitted with a fresh 64-hex qrToken; regB/regC read back still waitlisted -- PASS. AC2 -- 12h-out event: isAutoPromotionHalted returns true (12h<=24h); decidePromotionEligibility row 2 refuses 'halted-t24h' before step 4 is ever reached (no registrations SELECT against the waitlist at all, confirmed by reading the early-return at line 402-404); outcome is exactly {kind:'withdrawn',promotion:{kind:'halted-t24h'}}; freed seat stays free (admitted count 0) -- PASS. AC3 -- empty waitlist: step 4's SELECT ... LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE (lines 409-415) finds no row -> {kind:'no-waitlist'}, a normal return, not a throw; withdrawRegistration's own return is {kind:'withdrawn',promotion:{kind:'no-waitlist'}}, no error -- PASS. AC4 -- see above, PASS (20/20, re-run by me). AC5 -- decidePromotionEligibility row 1 (eventStatus!=='published' OR isFinished) refuses both a cancelled event and a finished event with 'event-not-eligible', checked before any registrations read -- confirmed by reading the two dedicated cases; waitlisted row read back unchanged in both -- PASS. AC6 -- withdraw.test.ts's real grammY bot.handleUpdate() dispatch case: promoted person's broadcast_opt_in explicitly set false beforehand, sendMessage still sent to THEIR OWN chat_id (verified via captured payload.chat_id) with promotion.admittedPrefix/qrLabel copy; withdrawer's own confirmedReply also sent unaffected -- confirmed by reading handlers/withdraw.ts's sendPromotionNotification (no broadcast_opt_in check anywhere in its path, matching S10's transactional-sends-ignore-the-flag rule by omission) -- PASS. AC7 -- exactly one registration.promote audit_log row per successful promotion (writeAuditLog reached only on the one write-worthy branch, same tx as the UPDATE, confirmed by construction at lines 424-437); re-running promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible against a still-full event returns {kind:'capacity-full'} both times with zero new audit writes -- PASS. Sentinel resolution judgment (BACKEND-DEV's flagged design/purity tension, MINOR issue in step-02): design §4 states WithdrawOutcome's 'withdrawn' member gains a mandatory `promotion: PromotionOutcome` field, but decideWithdrawOutcome is declared pure (no I/O) and cannot compute a real promotion outcome. BACKEND-DEV resolved this by having decideWithdrawOutcome's own 'withdrawn' return supply the design's OWN pre-existing {kind:'not-attempted'} sentinel (already defined by §0 step 7 for 'promotion was not attempted') rather than inventing new vocabulary. I traced the actual call path: withdrawRegistration (the impure function) calls decideWithdrawOutcome, and on 'withdrawn' it discards decideWithdrawOutcome's own `.promotion` field entirely -- it constructs and returns a FRESH `{kind:'withdrawn', promotion}` object (registration.ts line 563) where `promotion` is the real, freshly-computed PromotionOutcome from step 6/7, never the pure function's sentinel. So the sentinel value is observable ONLY by a direct unit test of decideWithdrawOutcome in isolation (registration.db.test.ts's own 'returns withdrawn for an eligible...' case, which now asserts the sentinel) -- it never reaches any real caller, any handler, or any user-visible behavior. This is a type-level accommodation with zero behavior impact, using only vocabulary the design itself already defines, and does not touch any capacity/consent/data-visibility rule. JUDGMENT: acceptable as implemented, correctly filed as MINOR rather than blocking or routed back to CODE-DESIGNER -- though I agree with BACKEND-DEV's own suggestion that a future design pass should either state this sentinel explicitly in §4 or give decideWithdrawOutcome's 'withdrawn' branch a narrower return type of its own (mirroring RegisterForEventResult sitting atop RegistrationOutcome) so this gap doesn't have to be silently bridged by an implementer again. Not escalating to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR since it is a documentation-completeness gap in the design, not an incorrect or unsafe implementation choice. T-24h evaluation-time discipline (decisions/0006): isAutoPromotionHalted(startsAt, evaluationTime) (event.ts lines 744-746) takes evaluationTime as an explicit parameter and performs no clock read of its own -- confirmed by reading the full function body (one arithmetic comparison, no `new Date()`, no SQL). decidePromotionEligibility and promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible both thread evaluationTime through as a parameter from their caller, ultimately withdrawRegistration's own `at` parameter, which handlers/withdraw.ts supplies as `new Date()` at the single call site (line 130) -- the only place the wall clock is read, at the top of the call chain, not inside any predicate. Grepped registration.ts and event.ts case-insensitively for now()/current_timestamp: no match in either file outside header-comment prose stating the negative constraint. writeAuditLog's `at` parameter use (an audit/bookkeeping write) is the one place a Date flows into a write without being compared -- exempted per decisions/0006's own closing paragraph. Compliant. Domain logic outside handler bodies (decisions/0004): read handlers/withdraw.ts in full (232 lines). makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler's only added logic beyond REQ-022's existing shape is a single `if (outcome.kind === 'withdrawn' && outcome.promotion.kind === 'promoted')` branch dispatch (line 140) to sendPromotionNotification -- no admission-state, eligibility, or capacity rule is evaluated here or inside sendPromotionNotification itself; that helper is composition only (resolve promoted user's own lang via existing resolveLang, fetch event title/date-time via existing getEventByIdWithChapterTimezone, join i18n catalog strings, call ctx.api.sendMessage) with one defensive null-tgId guard (a data-availability check, not a business rule). Every actual decision (decidePromotionEligibility, promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible, decideWithdrawOutcome) lives in domain/registration.ts and domain/event.ts, both framework-free -- confirmed no grammY import in either file (registration.ts's own import list, lines 1-12; event.ts's, lines 1-7). Compliant. Schema/migration review (decisions/0005, S13): confirmed `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/migrations apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` is empty -- no migration in this diff at all, matching the design's own §0 no-schema-change claim (independently re-checked against the current schema.ts: admission enum's existing values, registrations_waitlist_order_idx, qr_token all pre-date this run). Not applicable -- no SECURITY-REVIEWER migration sign-off needed for a migration, though S7/S8/S10 (capacity, consent-independent notification, PII exposure via sendMessage to a resolved tgId) remain mandatory review surface for Step 2c regardless. Workspace/build-output check: no new npm workspace, no apps/* rename, no build-output directory moved -- confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD --stat` (only existing files under apps/bot/src, i18n, docs, handoffs changed; no package.json touched). No scratch `docker build` required per my role file's trigger condition. COMMANDS RE-RUN MYSELF, REAL OUTPUT (repo root, scratch Postgres bot-postgres-1 already running from BACKEND-DEV's session, reused as-is): `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only, unchanged). `npm run build` -> exit 0, both workspaces clean (apps/web Next.js build succeeded, apps/bot's tsc -p tsconfig.json clean). `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -> 17 files / 211 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches BACKEND-DEV's reported count exactly, independently re-run by me. Also re-ran registration.db.test.ts + handlers/withdraw.test.ts together with --no-file-parallelism, --reporter=verbose -> 50/50 passed (all REQ-022 and REQ-023 cases individually confirmed green). Scope check: diff touches exactly the files the design named (domain/event.ts, domain/registration.ts + its test file, domain/user.ts, handlers/withdraw.ts + its test file, i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts) plus the design/handoff bookkeeping files -- confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD --stat`. No scope creep found. No stray file left in the project root or elsewhere -- confirmed `git status --porcelain` clean after deleting my own scratch test file.

ac_results.AC1: PASS -- registration.db.test.ts: 48h-out event, capacity full, 3 waitlisted at created_at+1s/+2s/+3s; withdrawal promotes exactly the earliest (regA) with a fresh qr_token; regB/regC untouched, still waitlisted
ac_results.AC2: PASS -- 12h-out event: isAutoPromotionHalted true, decidePromotionEligibility refuses 'halted-t24h' before any waitlist read; outcome {kind:'withdrawn',promotion:{kind:'halted-t24h'}}; freed seat stays free (admitted count 0)
ac_results.AC3: PASS -- empty waitlist: step 4 finds no row, returns {kind:'no-waitlist'} (not an error); withdrawRegistration returns {kind:'withdrawn',promotion:{kind:'no-waitlist'}}
ac_results.AC4: PASS -- re-run myself, 20/20 iterations, 815ms: admitted-row count never exceeded 1 racing promotion against a fresh registerForEvent for the same freed seat. NEW scenario I constructed (two concurrent withdrawals, shared waitlist of 2, 15 iterations): each freed seat promotes a distinct waitlisted person every time, no double-promotion, no lost promotion
ac_results.AC5: PASS -- promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible refuses both a cancelled event and a finished event with 'event-not-eligible', checked before any registrations read; waitlisted row unchanged in both cases
ac_results.AC6: PASS -- real grammY dispatch: promoted person (broadcast_opt_in=false) still receives sendMessage to their own chat_id; withdrawer's own reply unaffected; no broadcast_opt_in check exists anywhere in the notification path (S10 compliant by omission)
ac_results.AC7: PASS -- exactly one registration.promote audit_log row per successful promotion; re-running against a still-full event returns 'capacity-full' both times with zero new audit writes

evidence.lock_order_deadlock_check: CONFIRMED SAFE -- promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible's SELECT events FOR UPDATE (registration.ts lines 368-378) is the literal first statement in the function; withdrawRegistration never independently locks events (only its own registrations row, lines 508-518); the only resource both transactions ever contend for is the single events row, which structurally cannot produce a deadlock cycle regardless of the differing order of the second (non-shared) row each transaction locks afterward
evidence.dual_withdrawal_shared_waitlist_scenario: PASS, 15/15 iterations, independently constructed -- two concurrent withdrawals from the same capacity-2 event racing to promote from a shared 2-person waitlist: every iteration promoted both waitlisted users exactly once each (Set of promoted userIds always size 2, matching the two seeded candidates exactly), final state always 2 admitted/0 waitlisted -- confirms no double-promotion of the same candidate and no lost promotion under real contention on the per-row FOR UPDATE candidate lock (step 4), a scenario BACKEND-DEV's own AC4 test does not cover since it only races promotion against a fresh registerForEvent, not promotion against promotion
evidence.sentinel_resolution_judgment: ACCEPTABLE AS IMPLEMENTED, not routed back to CODE-DESIGNER -- traced the actual call path and confirmed decideWithdrawOutcome's {kind:'not-attempted'} sentinel on its 'withdrawn' branch is discarded by withdrawRegistration (which constructs a fresh return object with the real, I/O-derived promotion outcome, registration.ts line 563) and is therefore never observed by any real caller/handler/user-visible behavior -- only by a direct unit test of the pure function in isolation. A type-level accommodation with zero behavior impact, using only vocabulary the design already defines (the sentinel itself, §0 step 7). Correctly filed as MINOR by BACKEND-DEV rather than blocking; agree the design's §4 should be tightened in a future pass to state this explicitly or give decideWithdrawOutcome's 'withdrawn' branch a narrower type of its own, but this is a documentation-completeness gap in the design, not an incorrect or unsafe implementation choice, so it does not warrant CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR rework of this run

result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) -- mandatory, S7/S8/S10 all apply (capacity guarantee via the new events-row lock inside promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible; the promotion notification's unconditional bypass of broadcast_opt_in, which is intentional per S10's own transactional-sends table but should be independently confirmed against that table's exact wording; and the promoted person's tgId/lang being read and used to address a Telegram send to someone other than the acting ctx.from, the first call site in this codebase to do so). My own assessment: the diff introduces no new PII field, no new auth surface beyond the existing resolveActingUser/ownership gates already reviewed under REQ-022, and the one genuinely new structural element (a second FOR UPDATE lock acquisition, on events, from a code path -- promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible -- that did not exist before) I have independently traced for both lock-order-deadlock safety and double-promotion safety under real concurrency, including a scenario (two concurrent withdrawals against a shared waitlist) not covered by BACKEND-DEV's own tests. SECURITY-REVIEWER should still independently confirm rather than take this as sufficient, per this pipeline's re-derive rule, with particular attention to whether S10's transactional-sends table actually names waitlist-promotion notifications or whether that's an inference this design makes on its own.
